The key to understanding this situation is to look at the Julia set for the parabolic root points. Since the two root points of an A component are dual to each other, they have Julia sets which are identical, except for the choice of which component to label as *a* and which to label as *−a*. Nearly all of the examples we know are for rabbit regions. As one specific example, let us concentrate on the 1*/*3 -rabbit region as shown in Figure54, and on the A component in the upper left of this Figure. Figure60illustrates the Julia set for either of its two root points. (See Figure21for an analogous Julia set for the 1*/*2 rabbit, and Figure23for the 1*/*5 rabbit.) Given any co-periodic angle *θ* with denominator 3(3 *p* *−* 1), it is useful to consider the corresponding periodic angle 3*θ* with denominator 3 *p* *−*1. Note that two co-periodic angles *θ* and *θ* *′* satisfy 3*θ* = 3*θ* *′* if and only if they are twins. In our example, the root point of each *±*2*a* component in the Julia set is the landing point of six dynamic rays. However, only four of the six dynamic angles correspond to parameter angles for rays landing at the specified root point of A.
